policy.causal_rule: No XRP price effect, capital rotation, collateral utilization or adoption impact is inferred from corporate announcements, stablecoin supply changes, exchange freezes, ETF tracker totals or protocol releases without synchronized point-in-time flow evidence and out-of-sample testing.

edges.claim: Coinbase reported $22B average USDC held in its products and $307M stablecoin revenue in Q3 2026. These are company-wide USDC/stablecoin economics, not XRP-specific customer flows.
Coinbase began RLUSD access through Prime, Exchange and retail on Oct 28; deposits/withdrawals on XRPL, Base and Ethereum. Global Exchange collateral availability was future at announcement.
Circle made native USDC available on XRPL in June 2025 through Circle Mint and APIs without requiring a third-party bridge. This establishes Circle's direct operational presence on XRPL.
Circle reports $71.0B circulation and $71.2B reserves as of Oct 26, with -$4.2B net circulation over 30 days. Destination flows are unknown.

Ripple and Coinbase announced RLUSD distribution on Coinbase's Prime, Exchange and retail platforms; this is a commercial relationship around RLUSD, not evidence of Ripple equity ownership or XRP price causality.
Bitnomial Clearinghouse lists XRP collateral with a 40% haircut and $15M notional cap. This is a specific DCO rule and does not establish broad eligibility across all CFTC-regulated markets.
Bitnomial announced RLUSD margin deposits for institutional perpetuals, futures and options alongside XRP support, extending its Ripple relationship.
The CFTC's Dec 8, 2025 pilot release names BTC, ETH and USDC. XRP is not named in that announcement; this must be kept separate from Bitnomial's own XRP collateral rules.

Reuters reports Binance's investigation and issuer freezes: nearly $1.57B Tether, over $800M Circle and roughly $200M Ripple. The Ripple asset type is unidentified; frozen totals are reported, not audited recoveries.

XRPL issuer freeze controls apply to issued tokens, not native XRP. Custodial exchanges may restrict assets held in their own custody. Ripple's reported $200M freeze therefore cannot be labeled an on-ledger freeze of native XRP.
Alpha Finance's XRP-specific page uses 30 trading sessions while its cross-asset page uses 30 calendar days; different fund coverage and cutoff prevent direct comparison.

The 3.3.0 release contains six amendments; two substantive amendments are reported enabled, while ConfidentialTransfer, DynamicMPT and Sponsor remain below the activation threshold in two independent node snapshots. Release inclusion is not activation.
The channel and video candidates use Kamilah/Camila spelling variants; identity equivalence with the requested Camilla Stephenson is not established.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Coinbase's stablecoin, subscription/services, derivatives and prediction-market businesses may reduce reliance on spot transaction fees.
disconfirming_evidence: Transaction revenue still fell about 43% year-over-year.
Stablecoin revenue is exposed to USDC circulation and reserve yields; subscription/services may still correlate with crypto activity.
GAAP net income includes a large investment gain, so headline profit overstates recurring operating performance.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Circle's 30-day USDC contraction may reflect redemptions, treasury/payment seasonality or broad risk reduction rather than capital moving into XRP or RLUSD.
disconfirming_evidence: No matched issuer, wallet, exchange, OTC or ETF data connects USDC redemptions to XRP purchases.
USDC's XRPL deployment proves availability, not actual XRP bridge demand.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Issuer freezes may demonstrate institutional compliance capability and law-enforcement coordination while also exposing centralized stablecoin censorship/concentration risk.
disconfirming_evidence: Freeze amounts are reported, not independently audited; exact incident cause and customer loss remain unresolved.
The effect on user trust, redemptions and market liquidity has not been measured.

competing_hypotheses.claim: XRP collateral acceptance at Bitnomial may improve capital efficiency for institutional derivatives participants and create a use case for held XRP inventory.
disconfirming_evidence: 40% haircut and $15M notional cap constrain capacity.
Actual deposited collateral, usage, market-maker balances and incremental XRP demand are undisclosed.
This is venue-specific, not blanket CFTC approval.

competing_hypotheses.claim: XRP can be eligible collateral under a specific CFTC-registered clearinghouse rule even though it is not named in the CFTC's Dec 2025 digital-assets pilot announcement.
disconfirming_evidence: No evidence here that the CFTC pilot itself includes XRP.
No evidence that all FCMs, DCOs or clearing venues may accept XRP on the same terms.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Ripple's reported roughly $200M freeze likely concerns issued tokens or assets in custodial systems rather than a protocol-level freeze of native XRP.
disconfirming_evidence: Reuters does not identify the asset, chain, addresses or custody mechanism.
Native XRP may still be frozen by a centralized custodian at the account level even though no issuer can freeze it on-ledger.

competing_hypotheses.claim: The Alpha Finance ETF figures differ mainly because one uses 30 trading sessions and the other 30 calendar days, in addition to differing fund populations/cutoffs.
disconfirming_evidence: Fund-by-fund holdings, shares outstanding and creations/redemptions have not been reconciled.
Page refresh and late settlement corrections may still change the totals.

competing_hypotheses.claim: XRPL's new token privacy, sponsorship and dynamic MPT capabilities may improve institutional fit if amendments activate and real issuers deploy them.
disconfirming_evidence: ConfidentialTransfer, DynamicMPT and Sponsor remain below threshold in the observed Oct 29 snapshots.
Protocol capability does not prove enterprise adoption, liquidity or XRP demand.
No production deployment/usage metrics have been collected.
